text:
Lena Ortiz: Heads-up: CareAxis wants to consolidate two on-prem accounts (acct A -> acct B) as part of renewal and is asking to transfer the remaining platform promo credit to the consolidated account. We have HSM pass-throughs and a mid-term support tier change in the mix.
Marcus Green: Consolidations happen. Need to confirm contract language around non-transferable promos. Also check if the HSM line is vendor pass-through or a Redwood-managed add-on; impacts how we refund.
Lena Ortiz: From the ticket: they list invoice 202720 and 202721. Invoice snippets below.
```
Invoice 202720 (acct A renewal)
- Private deployment license: $35,000
- Platform fee (annual): $6,500
- Platform promo credit: -$1,300
- HSM vendor pass-through: $1,200
- Support (Standard): $6,000
Total: $47,400

Invoice 202721 (acct B renewal)
- Private deployment license: $85,000
- Platform fee (annual): $15,000
- Platform promo credit: -$4,000
- HSM vendor pass-through: $3,600
- Support (Premium -> Enterprise mid-term): $22,000
- Proration credit (support change): -$5,500
Total: $116,100
```
BillingBot: (automated) Received consolidation inquiry for account pair A->B and potential promo transfer. Scanning invoices and promo memos. Found platform promo memos tied to account-level promo_id P-9932 (applied to both accounts during original sales). Flagging case BLG-2026-2210 for manual review. Also note HSM pass-throughs are recorded with vendor_invoice_id V-558 and V-559.
Marcus Green: Key questions: (1) Are promo credits contractually transferrable on consolidation? (2) If we transfer, do we need to alter original invoice PDFs or create internal transfer memos? (3) How to handle HSM vendor pass-throughs if vendor invoice was paid twice after consolidation?
Legal - Anya: Quick read of the Master Services Agreement addendum: "Promotional credits are account-scoped and non-transferable unless explicit written consent from Redwood is provided." So transfer is allowed only if we approve. Also watch for anti-circumvention clauses around consolidation to extend promos beyond original term.
Finance - Greg: From an accounting perspective, transferring a promo credit between two customer accounts requires an inter-account adjustment and a memo that leaves the original invoice intact (we issue a credit note on acct A and an equivalent debit/credit on acct B). We cannot just edit historic invoices for audit trail reasons.
CS - Priya: Customer says they consolidated because they merged teams and want remaining promo balance (acct A has $1,300, acct B has $4,000). They ask to merge the unused promo amounts so consolidated promo = $5,300 applied to new renewal. They also want HSM pass-throughs to be collapsed and any duplicate vendor billing reversed.
Lena Ortiz: Proposed ops plan: (1) Approve promo transfer conditionally — require signed consolidation amendment acknowledging promo transfer and that no new promos will be issued. (2) Issue CN on acct A for $1,300 and create a memo/debit on acct B to add $1,300 to their balance (net effect: promo consolidated). (3) Reconcile vendor invoices V-558/V-559; if vendor billed twice, create vendor refund request and apply CN to customer if necessary. (4) Recalculate proration for support tier change on acct B to ensure -$5,500 is correct.
Marcus Green: Agree. Need Legal to approve amendment text and Finance to confirm ledger entries.
Legal - Anya: I can draft a short consolidation amendment stating: "Customer requests consolidation of accounts A and B. Redwood agrees to transfer remaining promotional credits totaling $1,300 from account A to account B, subject to the conditions that (i) credits remain non-transferable outside of this consolidation, (ii) credits apply only to outstanding/renewal invoices and expire per original terms, and (iii) this amendment is effective upon signature." Will send draft to CS and Lena.
Finance - Greg: Accounting flow: create credit note CN-9001 on acct A (-$1,300). Create adjustment on acct B showing applied promo +$1,300 (internal memo ID IM-2210). Ensure GL entries net to zero for revenue recognition. If vendor refunds are issued, process separate vendor ledger entries and then apply customer-facing credit if needed.
BillingBot: (automated) Queued CN-9001 for acct A pending Legal amendment and signed consolidation form. Flagged vendor invoices V-558 and V-559 for reconciliation; created vendor case VND-3321.
CS - Priya: I'll send the consolidation amendment to the customer and ask them to sign. Also confirming they want promo applied to the next invoice and prefer credits over cash refunds. I'll post their signed doc when returned.
Lena Ortiz: On HSMs: Marcus, please confirm whether we treated HSM as pass-through or product on acct A historically; we need that to decide refund path.
Marcus Green: Checked product catalog: acct A had HSM recorded as vendor pass-through (V-558). acct B HSMs were billed as vendor pass-throughs (V-559) too. So vendor billed us for both. If vendor only issued one invoice after consolidation, we should not double-charge customer. Omar from Billing Eng needs to check ingestion logs.
BillingBot: (automated) Billing Eng flag ENG-BILL-330 created to dedupe vendor pass-through ingestion. Attaching logs to case BLG-2026-2210.
Finance - Greg: Also watch the proration on acct B: support upgrade effective 2025-12-10; renewal 2026-02-01. The -$5,500 proration in invoice 202721 seems high; will recalc once we receive the signed amendment and final consolidation date.
Legal - Anya: One more note: make sure amendment references the original promo IDs and includes a clause stating the transfer is a one-time exception, for audit defense.
Lena Ortiz: Final ask items before we notify customer: (A) Legal amendment drafted and signed, (B) CN-9001 queued and approved, (C) vendor reconciliation confirming no double-bill or vendor refund path, (D) recalculated proration on acct B with reconciliation PDF. Once done, Finance will apply credits and Billing will reissue corrected renewal invoice for the consolidated account.
CS - Priya: Customer replied and signed the consolidation amendment this morning. Uploading signed PDF to the case.
BillingBot: (automated) Received signed amendment. CN-9001 now approved and created. Vendor case VND-3321 shows vendor confirmed single billing; V-559 was an import duplicate. Vendor issued refund to Redwood; awaiting posting. Vendor refund will be applied back to the customer's account as part of the consolidation settlement.
Finance - Greg: Vendor refund posted: VR-4472 for $3,600. We'll apply $3,600 to customer credit lines before applying promo transfer. Net customer credit after adjustments expected to be: existing promos $5,300 + vendor refund application (if applicable) less any proration debits. Will post final ledger snapshot.
Marcus Green: I've recalculated support proration for acct B: corrected proration should be -$3,200 (not -$5,500). That creates a debit of $2,300 back to the customer. Combining promo transfer + vendor refund + proration correction yields net credit ~ $6,400 (draft number). Greg, confirm final amount and create CN/CN offsets accordingly.
Finance - Greg: Reconciliation attached to case BLG-2026-2210: final net credit to customer = $6,400. CNs applied: CN-9001 (acct A) $1,300, CN-9002 (acct B) vendor refund pass-through application $3,600, PR-ADJ-2210 debit reversal $2,300. All ledger entries balanced. Corrected consolidated invoice 2027-CONSL issued showing net credit applied and new total.
CS - Priya: Customer acknowledged receipt and thanked us. They prefer credits applied to next renewal. No refund requested.
Lena Ortiz: Great work. Closing checklist: billing to reissue PDFs and mark case BLG-2026-2210 resolved once CNs applied and corrected invoice posted. BillingBot: close case when done.
BillingBot: (automated) Case BLG-2026-2210 resolved. Corrected consolidated invoice 2027-CONSL issued and CNs applied. Notifications sent to stakeholders.
Lena Ortiz: Thanks team :thumbsup\":
